newsitem.title: USA: McDonnell Douglas plans $40 mln learning center.
newsitem.headline: McDonnell Douglas plans $40 mln learning center.

text.p: McDonnell Douglas Corp plans to build a $40 million six-building learning center on an estate near St. Louis overlooking the Missouri River, the vice president for corporate communications said Wednesday.
McDonnell Douglas and Boeing Co hope to open the new learning center in 1999 on property purchased before they announced plans for a merger last year, Larry McCracken said.
Boeing has endorsed the plan, which has been modified to take into account the increased size and scope of the company for "a modern corporate university," McCracken said.
"This will be the center of our professional development training for the entire Boeing Co," McCracken said.
The St. Louis County Planning Commission has scheduled a public hearing on the proposal July 7.
The plans include a three-story 32,300 square foot education building, three 9,800-square foot lodges with small meeting spaces, a dining hall and a support building, McCracken said.
The center would also include a 182-space parking lot and possibly another 120 spaces in front of the mansion.
McDonnell Douglas had planned to build a facility on a different site in the late 1980s, but the plans never materialized.
Boeing and McDonnell Douglas hope to complete the merger by August 1 and begin operations August 4, McCracken said.
